grants.Description: Opening Summary
grants.Program Focus:
OPENING SUMMARY — WEEK OF OCTOBER 19 – 23, 2026

Week at a Glance:

A light week. Grants.gov carried nineteen new federal postings from October 17 through 22 (the six October 16 items were profiled in last week's October 19 update), and the strategic weight sits in three places: FEMA's $400,000,000 FY 2026 Flood Mitigation Assistance notice, ARPA-E's $45,000,000 UNLOCK subsurface program with concept papers due November 20, DOE's reopening of the $967,000,000 Grid Resilience State and Tribal Formula round, and a cluster of DOJ research and NIH center announcements. California's one new solicitation landed on the run day: CEC released GFO-26-503, the $46,144,000 Proposition 4 DEBA grid-reliability competition, with a pre-application workshop November 5 and applications due January 26, 2027; Cal OES has also flagged the FMA pass-through. Policy activity was heavier than the grant flow: the REAP overhaul took effect October 16, DOE opened the 45Z emissions-value process, and the White House issued a Section 232 wind-turbine proclamation, a DPA Title III petroleum determination and two executive orders touching NIH and housing grantmaking. Items marked "not previously covered" were posted October 6–8 and never profiled; they are included because they are still open.

Flood Mitigation and Resilience:

FEMA FY 2026 Flood Mitigation Assistance (DHS-26-MT-029-000-98) — $400,000,000 ($20M capability and capacity building; $260M localized flood risk reduction; at least $120M individual flood mitigation). Only states, territories and federally recognized tribes apply; cities, counties and special districts are subapplicants through Cal OES. Localized projects capped at $25,000,000 federal share; cost share 75/25, rising to 90% and 100% federal for repetitive-loss and severe-repetitive-loss properties. FEMA GO deadline February 26, 2027, 3:00 p.m. ET; Cal OES notice-of-interest dates are still TBD. Staff added this row to the Master Calendar on October 22.

Energy — Subsurface R&D:

ARPA-E UNLOCK (DE-FOA-0003630) — $45,000,000, awards $3,000,000–$5,000,000, about 12 awards, for stimulation, recovery, enhanced geothermal, in-situ mineral leaching and produced-water technologies in low-permeability formations; eligibility unrestricted. Companion SBIR/STTR notice DE-FOA-0003631 for small businesses (awards $323,090–$4,630,944). Listings close November 20, 2026 (concept papers); cost-share percentages and the submission time could not be read from the NOFO this week.

Energy — Grid Resilience Formula Funds:

DOE reopened the Grid Resilience State and Tribal Formula Grant Program (DE-FOA-0002736, Amendment 010) on October 20 with about $967,000,000 in additional formula funds; states, territories and federally recognized tribes apply directly by February 17, 2027, 11:59 p.m. EST, and utilities, cooperatives and municipal systems reach the money through their state energy office's subgrant round (CEC in California) or a tribe's direct award. Per-jurisdiction allocations and match terms are in the NETL allocation table, not yet read.

Transportation — Digital Corridors (Forecast):

FHWA signaled a new Great American Digital Corridors (GADC) competition through an October 19 information-collection notice (91 FR 66192): up to $20,000,000 for FY 2026, 100% federal share, cooperative agreements to states, local and tribal governments, transit agencies, toll authorities, MPOs, private entities and nonprofits for real-time work-zone and operating-condition data on the Federal-aid system. NOFO date not stated; comments on the forms due December 15, 2026.

Public Safety and Justice Research:

NIJ posted three FY 2026 research solicitations on October 22, each due November 30, 2026 (Grants.gov) / December 7 (JustGrants): Drones as First Responders (O-NIJ-2026-172805, $3,500,000), Elder Abuse, Neglect and Exploitation (O-NIJ-2026-172804, $1,800,000) and Violent Crime: Gangs and Organized Criminal Groups (O-NIJ-2026-172806, $3,000,000); no per-award cap, open to governments, universities, nonprofits and companies. BJA Missing and Unidentified Human Remains (O-BJA-2026-172716) — $3,079,954, up to $1,000,000 each, due December 2 / December 9; state and local applicants must include a chief-executive certification. Not previously covered: OVC Specialized Human Trafficking Assistance TTA (O-OVC-2026-172790, $5,000,000, two awards, universities, nonprofits and companies only, due December 1 / December 8).

Education and Research — NIH:

Five institutional announcements posted October 16–20: NIDCD's National Human Ear Resource Network (RFA-DC-28-001, $3,600,000, up to six U24 awards at $450,000 direct/year, first receipt March 5, 2027) and its coordinating center (RFA-DC-28-002, one award, due March 5, 2027); NIAID's Translational Centers Using Microphysiological Systems for Infectious Diseases (RFA-AI-28-012, about $15,000,000, 7–11 U54 awards, due January 29, 2027); the Immune Tolerance Network recompetition (RFA-AI-28-005, $27,000,000, one award, due January 29, 2027); and NIDA's R34 pilot-study program (PAR-28-093, $450,000 direct-cost cap, first receipt February 16, 2027). Not previously covered and still open: HEAL IMPOWR Research Centers (RFA-DA-28-011, $12,000,000, 6–8 awards) and BEACON Center (RFA-DA-28-012), both due January 26, 2027; HIV implementation science (RFA-AI-27-018, roughly $50,000,000 across institutes) and Human Virome pilot projects (RFA-RM-27-024, up to $100,000 direct), both with first receipt November 10, 2026. Foreign organizations are ineligible under every RFA listed here.

Defense Research — Early-Career Faculty:

DARPA Young Faculty Award 2027 (DARPARA2701) — base awards up to $500,000 over 24 months, Director's Fellowship up to a further $500,000, 18 topic areas; tenure-track assistant or associate professors and recently tenured faculty at U.S. institutions; FFRDCs, UARCs and national labs excluded. Executive summaries due November 5, 2026; full proposals January 13, 2027. No cost share.

Coastal and Riverine Restoration:

EPA Region 1 Southeast New England Program Innovative Restoration Grants (EPA-I-R1-SNEP-2026A) — $5,312,813, awards $250,000–$1,000,000, up to eight awards, projects must sit within the SNEP area of coastal Rhode Island and southeastern Massachusetts; 15% match in the NOFO (the listing wrongly says none); due December 11, 2026, 11:59 p.m. ET; webinar November 4. NOAA's Oceanic and Atmospheric Research FY 2027–2029 BAA (NOAA-OAR-BAA-2027-33939) is open on a rolling basis for research, education and CESU projects outside NOAA's standing competitions; no appropriated funds are attached.

Agriculture and Wildlife:

FWS Wolf Livestock Loss Compensation and Prevention (F26AS00088) — $1,350,000, awards $10,000–$675,000, 13 expected; state governments and federally recognized tribes only; 50% match; funds split equally between nonlethal prevention and depredation compensation; due January 15, 2027, 11:59 p.m. ET. The Region 8 contact covers California and Nevada.

Arts, Culture and Humanities — Community Reading:

NEA Big Read 2027–28 (administered by Arts Midwest; posted October 20) — $1,476,500, about 65 matching grants of $5,000–$30,000 for community-wide reading programs around the "Read Like a Champion" sports theme; libraries, universities, school districts, tribal organizations, museums and local-government departments; 1:1 non-federal match; Phase 1 eligibility review due January 12, 2027, full proposals January 26, 2027 (noon Central).

California and Other States:

CEC GFO-26-503, Distributed Electricity Backup Assets — DERs for Grid Reliability (released October 23) — up to $46,144,000 less state cost-share set-asides for water-utility projects, for new zero-emission storage, load-flexibility and microgrid assets that add supply or shed load during grid emergencies; applications due January 26, 2027, 11:59 p.m.; pre-application workshop November 5, 2026, 1:00–4:00 p.m.; written questions due November 13. Award range, eligible applicants and match are in the solicitation manual (draft terms: $2,000,000–$8,000,000 and 25% match — verify). Cal OES has posted the FY 2026 FMA California process (NOI and subapplication dates pending; scoping calls through ResilientCA@caloes.ca.gov). Texas Water Development Board's Water Supply Corporations Grant — $50,000,000, 100% grant, Texas water supply corporations only, due January 13, 2027 — was never covered and has live Q&A sessions October 28 and November 3. NY DEC's four Hudson River Estuary grant rounds ($1,250,000 combined, awards up to $200,000, 10–15% match) are due December 17, 2026.

Policy & Compliance Updates:

DOE opened the Section 45Z emissions-value request process (91 FR 65737) for clean-fuel pathways not in Treasury's table. A Section 232 proclamation on wind turbine imports (October 22) starts 180 days of negotiations with tariffs as the fallback. A DPA Title III determination (October 22) authorizes federal financial support for petroleum production, refining, pipeline, storage and marine-terminal capacity. EO "Advancing Women's Health" (91 FR, FR Doc. 2026-21666) directs NIH to stand up a Women's Health Division within 90 days. FCC reopened NEPA/NHPA review rules for wireless builds (91 FR 66062; comments November 18). EPA proposed Class VI primacy for Utah (91 FR 66662; comments December 7). FERC issued a draft NEPA policy statement for gas projects (comments November 16) and proposed LNG blanket authorizations (comments December 21). EO "Decreasing Housing Costs" (October 22) asks a HUD/FHFA task force whether federal grants can be conditioned on standardized local permitting. Reminder: EPA RAIN-2027-G01 bars FASC-listed drones under every EPA assistance agreement, retroactive to December 22, 2025. The 2 CFR 200 rewrite remains proposed and blocked by the CR rider through December 11, 2026; IRS Bulletins 2026-42 and 2026-43 carried no energy-credit guidance.

Watch List / Upcoming:

REAP: the final rule took effect October 16; comments due November 2, 2026; USDA has not yet announced the first application window, and the program page still says grant applications are not being accepted. DOE ETIPP community technical assistance (sixth cohort, opened August 13): applications close November 18, 2026 (support forms 11:59 p.m. MT) for coastal, island, Alaska, small (under 50,000) and tribal communities in an ETIPP region — in-kind national-lab planning support plus up to $20,000 (Strategic Energy Planning) or $50,000 (Deep Dive) in implementation funds; a Regional Partner consultation is required before applying and no California-specific partner is listed, so West Coast applicants should confirm coverage at ETIPP@nlr.gov. EPA DERA National 2026 (covered September 25): webinar October 28, questions due November 24, applications January 22, 2027. EPA FY 2027 Brownfields assessment, RLF and cleanup NOFOs are still "fall 2026" with no posting as of October 23. NSF MRI: no FY 2027 solicitation as of October 23 despite the previously announced October 15–November 16 window; NSF 23-519 remains archived. DoD SBIR/STTR FY 2027 Release 1: pre-released October 7, opens October 28, closes November 25 (SBIR.gov copies; the Navy site shows 12:00 p.m. ET) — dodsbirsttr.mil did not render, so confirm there. Bureau of Reclamation: comments on the WTR 11-01 Title XVI feasibility-study revisions due October 29, 2026 (mmenendez@usbr.gov); revised requirements apply to studies submitted after January 15, 2027. NRCS California: first FY 2027 EQIP/CSP/ACEP batching date November 6, 2026, 5:00 p.m. PST. BJA RSAT formula (O-BJA-2026-172763, about $26,285,604, states only, due November 20): states must pass at least 10% through to local jails, so county sheriffs reach it as subrecipients of the state agency. USDA RUS ARC Program is now on Grants.gov (RUS-ARC-2026, posted October 19; LOIs close November 20, 11:59 a.m. ET). USDA Distance Learning and Telemedicine: page updated October 21 — not accepting applications due to funding constraints. HHS ACL FY 2027 forecasts posted October 19: Dementia Capability in Indian Country (HHS-2027-ACL-AOA-ADPI-0010, est. $1.7M, $200,000–$300,000, tribes and tribal organizations, est. post March 1, 2027), Elder Justice Innovation Grants (est. $3.5M, $250,000–$500,000, est. post March 15, 2027) and No Wrong Door System Modernization (est. $4.5M, $450,000, est. post January 17, 2027). NICHD forecasts (RFA-HD-28-001, -005, -006) have estimated posting July 24, 2027. State Justice Institute FY 2027 Grant Guideline (91 FR 66599): quarterly deadlines November 1, February 1, May 1, August 1; project grants up to $300,000 with dollar-for-dollar match; AI in court processes is a stated priority. California: CEC GFO-25-603 confirmed at November 20, 2026 and the Master Calendar now matches; the calendar's August 24 "[UPCOMING] DEBA" row should be replaced with the GFO-26-503 row in this week's additions sheet; CORE FY 2026-27 and Texas THIVE have no new dates; the DWR Urban Streams workshop on October 28 could not be re-verified on DWR's site. CTC's SB 1 cycle closes November 18 (LPP), 19 (SCCP) and 20 (TCEP). Inconsistencies to confirm: NOAA OAR BAA closes September 30, 2029 on the listing but September 30, 2028 in the BAA text; FEMA's separate FY 2026 Swift Current announcement could not be read (fema.gov pages fail to render); the UNLOCK concept-paper time (9:30 a.m. ET) and cost-share tiers come only from a consultant tracker. Continuing resolution expires December 11, 2026.

grants.Description: FEMA — Fiscal Year 2026 Flood Mitigation Assistance (FMA)
grants.Agency / Funder: Department of Homeland Security, FEMA — Resilience, Hazard Mitigation Assistance Division. Contact: FEMA GO Help Desk, femago@fema.dhs.gov, 877-585-3242. California subapplicants: Cal OES Hazard Mitigation, ResilientCA@caloes.ca.gov (scoping calls).
grants.Total Funding: $400,000,000 — Capability and Capacity Building $20,000,000; Localized Flood Risk Reduction Projects $260,000,000; Individual Flood Mitigation Projects at least $120,000,000. About 40 applicant awards and roughly 725 subawards anticipated.
grants.Award Range: Per-applicant range not stated. Subapplication caps: project scoping up to $500,000 federal share; localized flood risk reduction projects up to $25,000,000 federal share each; mitigation plans up to $100,000 per applicant (state plan $50,000; local plan $25,000); state technical assistance up to $50,000; individual property projects have no stated cap, but FEMA may rank lower where the average federal share exceeds $250,000 per unit (elevation) or $750,000 per unit (acquisition). Management costs: 10% recipients, 5% subrecipients.
grants.Eligible Applicants: Applicants: states, the District of Columbia, U.S. territories and federally recognized tribes only. Cities, counties, townships, special district governments and tribal nations are subapplicants through their state (Cal OES in California). All must participate in the NFIP and be in good standing; structures must have carried an NFIP policy before the application period opened on October 22, 2026; a current FEMA-approved hazard mitigation plan is required.
grants.Deadline: February 26, 2027, 3:00 p.m. ET in FEMA GO (state applications). Cal OES notice-of-interest and subapplication deadlines: TBD — Cal OES says its state notice follows "in the coming days".
grants.Program Focus: Reduces repetitive flood damage to NFIP-insured structures: community-scale drainage and flood-control projects, acquisition and elevation of repetitive-loss properties, project scoping, mitigation planning and state capability building. Scoring favors communities with high NFIP policy counts, repetitive-loss inventories, recent claims above $1,000,000, CRS participation and a 4:1 benefit-cost ratio. For California cities, counties, flood-control and levee districts this is the main federal flood-mitigation vehicle of the year; the window is long but Cal OES will set earlier internal dates. Action: identify repetitive-loss inventories now, confirm NFIP standing and plan currency, and request a Cal OES scoping call before the state NOI opens. Good material for a resilience-focused outreach campaign to coastal and riverine jurisdictions.
grants.Cost Share / Match: Federal share up to 75%; up to 90% for repetitive-loss properties; up to 100% for severe-repetitive-loss properties; non-federal share waived for insular areas under $200,000.
grants.Primary Sector: Hazard Mitigation; Flood Mapping; Civil Infrastructure and Resilience; State & Local Government; Tribal Programs
grants.Posting Date: October 22, 2026 (listing Version 2; NOFO file dated October 16, 2026). Staff added this program to the Master Calendar on October 22, so it is not repeated in this week's calendar additions sheet.

grants.Description: DOE ARPA-E — Unlocking New Levels of Output and Capacity for Key Subsurface Resources (UNLOCK)
grants.Agency / Funder: U.S. Department of Energy, Advanced Research Projects Agency-Energy. Contact: ARPA-E GO, arpa-e-co@hq.doe.gov; eXCHANGE help desk ExchangeHelp@hq.doe.gov. No individual program director is named on the listing.
grants.Total Funding: $45,000,000 (listing). A consultant tracker states the total is shared with the SBIR/STTR companion notice; the NOFO could not be read this week to confirm.
grants.Award Range: $3,000,000–$5,000,000; about 12 awards expected (listing).
grants.Eligible Applicants: Unrestricted — universities, companies, nonprofits, national labs (as team members) and state entities; see NOFO Section II.A. Teaming across operators, service companies and research institutions is the expected model.
grants.Deadline: Listing closes November 20, 2026 (concept papers). Time of day: 9:30 a.m. ET per a consultant tracker only — confirm in eXCHANGE. Full applications follow encourage/discourage notices, expected around January 2027 (unverified).
grants.Program Focus: Applied R&D on technologies that raise recovery and capacity from low-permeability, geologically complex formations: stimulation and fracture-network control, proppants, enhanced oil recovery in unconventionals, refracturing and well interference, produced-water management and far-field sensing (Category A, where most awards are expected), plus enhanced geothermal systems, in-situ leaching of minerals and metals, and coalbed methane (Category B). Fit: geothermal developers, critical-minerals and oilfield-technology companies, and the engineering and earth-science departments that partner with them. The three-week concept-paper window is the gate; a two-page concept paper is enough to stay in the running. Action: alert subsurface, geothermal and mining-technology contacts this week and offer concept-paper drafting.
grants.Cost Share / Match: Required (listing). Percentages not readable this week; a consultant tracker shows 20% standard, 5% for university, nonprofit and FFRDC-only teams, and 0% for small businesses in the first 12 months then 10% — treat as unverified until the NOFO is read.
grants.Primary Sector: Subsurface Resources; Geothermal; Critical Minerals; Research & Development; Energy

Pairs with CEC GFO-26-503 and the Cal OES FMA process below for a grid-and-flood resilience outreach theme.

grants.Cost Share / Match: Not stated on the pages read; the statute's state match and small-utility match terms were not confirmed this week.

grants.Description: National Institute of Justice — NIJ FY 2026 Research and Evaluation on Drones as First Responders
grants.Agency / Funder: U.S. Department of Justice, Office of Justice Programs, National Institute of Justice. Contact: OJP Response Center, OJP.ResponseCenter@usdoj.gov, 800-851-3420 (TTY 202-353-5556), 9 a.m.–5 p.m. ET.
grants.Total Funding: $3,500,000
grants.Award Range: No per-award floor or ceiling — budgets are set by the proposed research, up to the program total; 5–6 awards expected. (The listing shows the program total in the award-maximum field.)
grants.Eligible Applicants: State, county, city, township and special district governments; federally recognized and other tribal governments and organizations; public and private universities; independent school districts; nonprofits with or without 501(c)(3) status; small businesses and other for-profits. Non-U.S. entities are ineligible; one applicant per project — partners join as subrecipients.
grants.Deadline: Grants.gov SF-424: November 30, 2026, 11:59 p.m. ET; JustGrants full application: December 7, 2026, 8:59 p.m. ET. Awards anticipated by February 1, 2027.
grants.Program Focus: Rigorous evaluations of law-enforcement drone-as-first-responder programs — existing deployments or new pilots — covering violent-crime response, immigration-enforcement support and other operations, with cost-benefit analysis and archived data; agencies may keep drone equipment bought with grant funds. A research partner is required, so the natural structure is a university or evaluation firm as applicant with a police or sheriff's department as site, or the agency as applicant with the researcher as subrecipient. Period of performance up to 36 months. Action: match criminal-justice research faculty with agencies already running or planning DFR programs; pair with the FEMA Counter-UAS item covered last week for a public-safety technology conversation.
grants.Primary Sector: Public Safety; Law Enforcement; Research & Development

grants.Description: Bureau of Justice Assistance — BJA FY 2026 Missing and Unidentified Human Remains (MUHR) Program
grants.Agency / Funder: U.S. Department of Justice, Office of Justice Programs, Bureau of Justice Assistance. Contact: OJP Response Center, OJP.ResponseCenter@usdoj.gov, 800-851-3420.
grants.Total Funding: Up to $3,079,954; 4 awards expected.
grants.Award Range: Up to $1,000,000 per award (the listing places this figure in the award-minimum field).

grants.Deadline: January 13, 2027, 11:59 p.m. CST through the TWDB online application. Live Q&A sessions October 28 and November 3, 2026.
grants.Program Focus: A rare 100% grant for small rural Texas water systems: supply, conservation and water-loss mitigation projects. Fit: GMA's Texas rural utility and water contacts and the engineering firms that serve water supply corporations. Posted before the window (the earliest dated item is a September 21 webinar) and never covered; included because the Q&A sessions fall inside the next two weeks.
grants.Primary Sector: Water; Rural Water and Wastewater; Rural Communities
grants.Posting Date: Not stated on the page; webinar September 21, 2026 — not previously covered.

grants.Description: NYS DEC Hudson River Estuary Program — 2026 Grants: Tributary Restoration and Resiliency, Local Stewardship Planning, River Education, River Access
grants.Opportunity #: SFS bid events HRE50-2026 (Tributary Restoration and Resiliency), HRER51 (Local Stewardship Planning), HRER52 (River Education), HRER49 (River Access)
grants.Agency / Funder: New York State Department of Environmental Conservation, Hudson River Estuary Program (Environmental Protection Fund). Contact: Susan Pepe, grants coordinator, HREPgrants@dec.ny.gov; program office 845-256-3016.
grants.Total Funding: $1,250,000 across the four rounds: Tributary Restoration about $400,000; Local Stewardship Planning about $350,000; River Education about $250,000; River Access about $250,000.
grants.Award Range: Tributary Restoration $10,500–$200,000; Local Stewardship Planning $10,500–$50,000; River Education $20,000–$100,000; River Access $10,500–$100,000.
grants.Eligible Applicants: Municipalities (counties, cities, towns, villages), tribal nations, public authorities and benefit corporations, soil and water conservation districts, school districts, colleges and universities, and 501(c)(3) nonprofits (prequalified in the Statewide Financial System). Projects must sit within the Hudson River Estuary program boundary and advance the 2026–2030 Action Agenda.
grants.Deadline: December 17, 2026, 3:00 p.m. ET for all four, submitted in the NYS Statewide Financial System. Webinars were held October 8 (recordings posted).
grants.Program Focus: Dam removal and culvert replacement design and construction (priority to river herring and eel passage), climate-adaptation and watershed planning, environmental education facilities and programs, and resilient public river-access improvements. Small awards but reliable annual rounds that pair well with FEMA and state resilience funding as match. Fit: GMA's New York municipal, nonprofit and university contacts in the Hudson Valley. Bid period opened September 23 and the ENB notices ran October 7; not previously covered.
grants.Cost Share / Match: Tributary Restoration and River Access at least 10% (15% scores higher); Local Stewardship Planning and River Education at least 15% (25% scores higher); other state or federal funds may not count toward the education match.
grants.Primary Sector: Restoration; Habitat Connectivity; Climate; Outdoor Access; Environmental and Cultural Education; State & Local Government
grants.Link to Solicitation: DEC grants page; Tributary Restoration RFA; Local Stewardship Planning RFA; River Education RFA; River Access RFA
grants.Posting Date: September 23, 2026 (bid period); ENB notices October 7, 2026 — not previously covered.

grants.Description: DOE — Section 45Z Clean Fuel Production Credit: Emissions Value Request Process Now Open (Notice of Availability)
grants.Issuing Agency: U.S. Department of Energy, Office of Critical Minerals and Energy Innovation. Contact: John Cabaniss, 45ZEmissionsRequest@doe.gov, 202-287-5531.
grants.Effective Date: Process open on publication, October 16, 2026; no comment period.
grants.Summary: DOE's portal now accepts requests from transportation-fuel producers whose fuel, feedstock or pathway is not in Treasury's 45Z emissions-rate table. DOE issues an emissions value that the producer then uses to petition IRS for a provisional emissions rate under Notice 2025-10 and the February 2026 proposed rules. No processing-time commitment is stated. This is the missing step for non-table pathways to claim the credit.
grants.Who It Affects: Sustainable aviation fuel, renewable diesel, renewable natural gas, ethanol and other clean-fuel producers — companies, cooperatives and tribal fuel ventures — and the lenders and tax-equity partners who underwrite them.
grants.GMA Action Items: For clean-fuel clients with novel pathways, start the DOE request now and sequence it ahead of the IRS petition; note in client memos that credit value depends on this step. Coordinate with tax counsel; GMA does not give tax opinions.

grants.Description: White House — Section 232 Proclamation on Imports of Wind Turbines and Their Parts and Components
grants.Reference #: Proclamation signed October 22, 2026 (Federal Register citation pending)
grants.Issuing Agency: Executive Office of the President; Department of Commerce and USTR to negotiate.
grants.Effective Date: October 22, 2026; Commerce and USTR report within 180 days (about April 2027).
grants.Summary: Finds that wind turbine and component imports threaten national security but imposes no new tariff now (components remain subject to the existing steel, aluminum and copper 232 tariffs). Directs negotiations with trading partners; if no agreement is reached or it proves ineffective, the President may impose tariffs or other measures. Commerce continues monitoring.
grants.Who It Affects: Wind developers, utilities, electric cooperatives and tribes with onshore or offshore wind in interconnection queues; 45Y and 48E projects relying on imported nacelles and blades; port and manufacturing grant applicants tied to the wind supply chain.
grants.GMA Action Items: Add a tariff-risk line to wind project budgets and cost narratives in pending DOE, USDA and EDA applications; flag domestic-content positioning for 45Y/48E bonus credits; calendar the 180-day report.

grants.Description: White House — Defense Production Act Title III Determination on Domestic Petroleum Production, Refining and Logistics Capacity
grants.Reference #: Presidential Determination under DPA Section 303, October 22, 2026 (Federal Register citation pending)
grants.Issuing Agency: Executive Office of the President; delegated to the Secretary of War (DPA Title III program).
grants.Summary: Invokes DPA Section 303(a)(5) and waives the usual Section 303 limits (including the $50,000,000 threshold and congressional-notice requirements) to authorize purchases, purchase commitments and financial support for production capability in exploration and production, pipelines, storage and marine terminals, tied to the energy emergency declared in EO 14156. No dollar amount is stated.
grants.Who It Affects: Midstream, refining and marine-terminal operators; ports with fuel terminals; industrial-base contractors; California and Gulf Coast port and industrial clients.
grants.GMA Action Items: Watch SAM.gov and the DoD DPA Title III office for solicitations or other-transaction calls on fuel logistics; brief port and terminal clients that DPA financial support can take the form of grants, purchase commitments or loans.

grants.Description: White House — Executive Order: Advancing Women's Health To Improve Outcomes in All Phases of Life
grants.Reference #: FR Doc. 2026-21666 (EO number pending in the Federal Register)
grants.Issuing Agency: Executive Office of the President; HHS and NIH implement.
grants.Effective Date: Signed October 19, 2026; published October 22, 2026; NIH division due within 90 days (about January 17, 2027).
grants.Summary: Directs HHS to establish a Women's Health Division within an NIH institute within 90 days to fund and coordinate research (including replication studies), expand review of understudied conditions, increase inclusion of women in trials and enforce the sex-as-a-biological-variable policy through grantee accountability. Creates a White House Women's Health Task Force (HHS, USDA, DOL, ED, VA, EPA, FDA, CDC, NIH, ARPA-H, CMS) to direct grantmaking priorities toward prevention, treatment and long-term health. Revokes EO 14120. Subject to appropriations.
grants.Who It Affects: Universities, academic medical centers and research nonprofits applying to NIH, ARPA-H and CDC; current NIH grantees (SABV compliance).
grants.GMA Action Items: Expect new NIH NOFOs and notices of special interest in women's health in the first half of 2027; advise university clients to check SABV language in pending applications and position women's-health research teams now.

grants.Description: FCC — Modernizing the Commission's National Environmental Policy Act Rules (Further Notice of Proposed Rulemaking)
grants.Summary: Seeks comment on whether building and operating communications facilities is an NHPA Section 106 "undertaking" or an ESA "agency action", on batching Tower Construction Notification System submissions, bringing non-compliant towers into compliance for collocation, streamlining post-disaster rebuilds, and shortening tribal consultation and notification timelines (including the 15-day phone follow-up).
grants.Who It Affects: BEAD and ReConnect subgrantees, wireless ISPs, tower builders, counties and tribes (THPOs) that rely on the consultation process.
grants.GMA Action Items: Broadband clients with tower-heavy builds should consider filing comments on the review timelines; tribal clients should weigh in on consultation changes; note the possible schedule relief in BEAD deployment plans.

grants.Description: EPA — Utah Underground Injection Control Program: Class VI Primacy (Proposed Rule)
grants.Issuing Agency: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, Office of Water.
grants.Effective Date: Comments due December 7, 2026; one virtual hearing during the comment period (date on EPA's Utah Class VI page).
grants.Summary: Proposes to let Utah's Division of Oil, Gas and Mining permit and enforce Class VI carbon-sequestration wells (excluding Indian lands) under 40 CFR 147.2250, with EPA oversight through quarterly and annual reports — the fourth western state primacy action in a year, following Colorado's final approval covered last week.
grants.Who It Affects: Carbon capture and storage developers; ethanol, cement and power facilities in Utah; 45Q claimants; CEC GFO-26-502 industrial-carbon-capture applicants weighing out-of-state storage.
grants.GMA Action Items: For CCS clients with Utah projects, note the faster state permitting path and consider comments; keep the state-primacy map current in CCS client memos.

grants.Description: FERC — Draft Policy Statement on Environmental Review of Natural Gas Act Applications, and Proposed Blanket Authorizations at LNG Plants
grants.Effective Date: Policy statement comments due November 16, 2026, 5:00 p.m. ET (implementation only); LNG blanket-authorization comments due December 21, 2026.
grants.Summary: The draft policy statement would drop FERC's air-dispersion modeling requirement for compressor stations and LNG facilities in favor of Clean Air Act and state permit compliance, as part of a post-Seven County NEPA proportionality effort (one commissioner dissented). The proposed rule would auto-authorize minor in-footprint work at LNG plants, allow capacity increases and projects on up to 25 acres outside the footprint by 60/90-day prior notice, and phase out the Section 2.55 replacement option.
grants.Who It Affects: Pipeline and LNG applicants, gas utilities and the communities and intervenors near those facilities; indirectly, DOE-funded gas-grid projects.
grants.GMA Action Items: Minor for most GMA clients; relevant for utility and industrial clients with gas interconnections and for environmental-justice intervenors. No action unless a client has a pending FERC matter.

grants.Description: White House — Executive Order: Decreasing Housing Costs for the American People
grants.Reference #: Executive Order signed October 22, 2026 (number and Federal Register citation pending)
grants.Issuing Agency: Executive Office of the President; HUD and FHFA lead a task force with USDA, Commerce and VA.
grants.Effective Date: October 22, 2026; task-force recommendations due within 180 days (about April 2027).
grants.Summary: Creates a manufactured-housing task force to recommend, among other things, whether federal grant funding can be conditioned on or used to reward state and local standardized permitting; directs USDA and VA to lower direct single-family loan rates; launches FHFA mortgage-insurance cancellation and title pilots. No CDBG or HOME directives yet.
grants.Who It Affects: Cities and counties (future permitting conditions on HUD and other grants), housing authorities, rural housing lenders and USDA Section 502 borrowers.
grants.GMA Action Items: Watch for permitting conditions in 2027 HUD and USDA NOFOs (PRO Housing-type programs especially); brief city planning contacts that streamlined permitting may become a scoring factor.

grants.Description: EPA — RAIN-2027-G01: Prohibition on FASC-Listed Unmanned Aircraft Systems Under EPA Assistance Agreements (Reminder; not previously covered)
grants.Reference #: RAIN-2027-G01 (implements OMB Memorandum M-26-02 and the American Security Drone Act)
grants.Issuing Agency: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, Office of Grants and Debarment.
grants.Summary: Prohibits purchasing or operating drones made by entities on the Federal Acquisition Security Council's Covered Foreign Entity List under any EPA assistance agreement, including drones already bought and including State Revolving Fund borrowers. Recipients must screen manufacturers against the FASC list in SAM.gov, document the search in the award file, and pass-through entities must notify subrecipients.
grants.Who It Affects: Every EPA grantee and subrecipient — states, water and wastewater utilities, air districts, tribes, universities and nonprofits — that uses drones for monitoring, inspection or mapping.
grants.GMA Action Items: Add the FASC screen to EPA award-compliance checklists for current clients; tell SRF borrowers and air-district clients now; expect the same term to spread to DOT, DOE and USDA awards.
